_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoking: Building this week's brief of buying asks...

description: Use this when the user asks for a weekly brief or for this week only, such as "weekly brief for SEO audit" or "did anyone ask for bookkeeping this week?". Pass service, for example {"service": "bookkeeping"}, and optionally keywords and sources. Returns one summary line, counts by source and by day, and the top 10 posts with link, date, short quote, score, label, reason and reply_angle. The window is fixed to the last 7 days, with the same rules and sources as find_buying_intent. Not for a longer lookback or a set limit: use find_buying_intent for those. A quiet week returns no_data. Reddit is not searched.

keywords.description: Optional extra words a post must also contain, such as "shopify" or "small business" (up to 5). Every keyword must appear in a post, so a long list returns little. Leave it out for a first look and add one word only to narrow

service.description: The service you sell, not a company or person. Example call: {"service": "SEO audit"}. "alternative" alone, with no keywords, finds asks to replace any tool. Also try the person form (bookkeeper)

sources.description: Which public sources to read: hackernews (comments and Ask HN), hn_hiring (company posts in the newest monthly Hacker News "Who is hiring?" thread), github (open and closed issues) and stackexchange. Default is all four. Leave one out to skip it, for example stackexchange when it is rate limited

name: weekly_brief

as_of.description: ISO 8601 time the data was published by its source or fetched from it. A cached answer keeps the time of its fetch.

attribution.description: CC BY-SA attribution for Stack Exchange text

by_day.description: Intent posts per day, oldest first

how_scored.description: The scoring rules, so the user can see why a post scored as it did

message.description: The next step when status is not ok or a source was skipped, such as a longer lookback_days, the person form of the service, or leaving stackexchange out of sources

notice.description: What a score does and does not mean. Pass it on

source.description: Who the data comes from, to cite and to check it against.

sources_unavailable.description: Sources that could not be read and are missing from the answer

status.description: ok: posts found. no_data: no post asked for the service; message says what to try. unavailable: no source could be read; message says whether to retry or skip stackexchange

summary.description: One line: how many asks this week and from where

top_asks.description: The strongest intent posts of the week, up to 10

intent_score.description: 0 to 100 from the rules in how_scored. 40 or more is intent; a casual complaint scores 15

lead_source.description: Which buying-signal source this lead is, to store with the lead: hiring-for-supported-roles (a company job post), tool-recommendation-asks (asks for a pick or an alternative), solution-complaints (only complains), community-questions (any other ask)

quote.description: A quote of the ask, under 15 words

rank.description: Position by intent_score, 1 is the strongest

reason.description: One line naming the rules that matched

reply_angle.description: One line on what to reply. It never names the tool or the subject, so open the link to read it. Picked by rule from the strongest cue: thanks (check the thread first), a budget, a hire, a named friction, an alternative, a recommendation, or a complaint with no ask

signals.description: Labels of the rules that matched, such as "looking for", "budget stated", "wants to hire" or "company job post names the service"

source.description: Where the post is: hackernews, hn_hiring (the monthly hiring thread), github or stackexchange

url.description: Link to the post. For Stack Exchange this link is also the CC BY-SA attribution

title: Weekly brief of buying asks
